en: not skilled at doing something, as in bad at math
why: I'm bad at ~ is everyday speech; no sense covers lack of skill

en: no longer fresh and not safe to eat or drink
why: food going bad is common; harmful/poor-quality senses do not say spoiled

en: a short holiday from school or work, such as spring break
why: spring/winter break means 방학, which 쉬는 시간 does not convey

en: used in questions to ask someone to do something for you
why: Can you ...? is the most common spoken request; only ability and permission exist

en: used with not to say you are sure something is not true
why: That can't be right is very common; no possibility sense exists

en: to hear or understand something someone says
why: I didn't catch your name is everyday speech; absent

en: used to politely ask if you may do something
why: Could I ...? asks permission; existing request sense asks others to act

en: to pay for something, often for someone else
why: I'll cover it / cover the bill is common; absent

en: used before a verb to give it extra emphasis, as in I do like it
why: emphatic do is frequent in speech and confuses learners; absent

en: not working for a period of time, used about computers or systems
why: the internet is down is common; only mood sense exists for adjective

en: to choose to see someone's posts on social media
why: very common modern spoken use; absent

en: because of or in return for something, as in thanks for
why: Thanks for / sorry for are constant; no reason sense exists

en: considering what is usual for a type of person or thing
why: He's tall for his age is common; absent

en: in a way that is good enough or without problems
why: It works fine / I'm doing fine use fine as an adverb; only adjective exists

en: to make someone pay money as a punishment
why: I got fined is common; only the noun exists

en: to arrive at or reach a place
why: get home / get there is among the most frequent uses; absent

en: to buy or bring something for yourself or someone else
why: Can I get you a drink? / I'll get coffee; obtain/receive does not cover fetching or buying

en: used as be going to to talk about the future or a plan
why: be going to is core spoken future; absent

en: to belong in a particular place or fit into a space
why: Where does this go? is everyday; absent

en: used as I'm good to politely say you do not need anything
why: I'm good is the common polite refusal; no sense covers it

en: to suffer from an illness, pain, or other health problem
why: I have a cold/headache is constant; 가지다 is not how Korean says it

en: to arrange for someone to do something for you
why: I had my hair cut is a common causative pattern; absent

en: to keep something for someone so that it is available later
why: Can you hold my bag / hold a seat is common; absent

en: to put your arms around someone, such as a baby or a loved one
why: hold the baby / hold me is common; 잡다 does not cover embracing

en: using a particular language or way of doing something
why: Say it in English is everyday for learners; absent

en: used to add emphasis, as in it's just amazing
why: emphatic just is very frequent; 그냥/단지 does not cover it

en: used informally to fill a pause or when you are not exact
why: filler like is extremely common in casual speech; absent

en: in the same way as, or as if, as in like I said
why: like I said / looks like it's raining use like as a conjunction; absent

en: used to get attention before saying something important
why: Look, I'm sorry is everyday speech; absent

en: used as a lot to mean very much or much more
why: I like it a lot / a lot better is adverbial; only the noun sense exists

en: to do or perform an action, such as a mistake or a decision
why: make a mistake/decision/call is constant; Korean uses 하다, not 만들다

en: to be careful of something, as in mind your head
why: Mind your step/head is common in British speech; absent

en: taken away from the usual price, as in twenty percent off
why: 20% off is everyday shopping language; absent

en: not quite right, or no longer fresh, used about food or feelings
why: Something's off / the milk is off is common; absent

en: using a device or being broadcast by it, as in on TV or on the phone
why: on TV / on the phone is everyday; 위에 does not cover it

en: available to the public, such as a new movie or product
why: Is the movie out yet? is common; absent

en: used to say you agree or understand
why: Right. as agreement is constant in speech; absent

en: used at the end of a statement to check that it is true
why: ..., right? is the most common spoken tag question; absent

en: to go somewhere quickly or for a short time
why: I need to run to the store is common; absent

en: to flow, or to let water flow, as in my nose is running
why: runny nose / run the water is everyday; absent

en: used to give an example or a rough number
why: Let's meet at, say, seven is common; absent

en: to be in a romantic relationship with someone
why: Are you seeing anyone? is common; 만나다 alone is ambiguous

en: used to start a new topic or to move a conversation on
why: So, how was your trip? is constant; result sense does not cover opening a topic

en: used before a verb to say the same is true of someone else
why: So do I / So am I is everyday; absent

en: used informally to emphasize a statement, as in it sure is hot
why: It sure is is common American speech; 물론 is only agreement

en: to travel by a bus, train, taxi, or other vehicle
why: take the bus/subway is everyday; absent as a sense

en: to study a subject or do a test
why: take a class / take a test is everyday for students; absent

en: to the degree that is mentioned or understood, as in not that bad
why: It's not that bad is very common; absent

en: to the degree shown or mentioned, as in about this big
why: this big / this late is common with gestures; absent

en: before the hour when saying the time, as in ten to five
why: ten to five is the usual spoken way to tell time; absent

en: finished, used about a period of time, as in time's up
why: Time's up is everyday; absent

en: to look after someone or something for a short time
why: Can you watch my bag/kids? is common; absent

en: used to talk about things that happened often in the past
why: habitual would (we would go fishing) is common in storytelling; absent
